candidates.title: AI is transforming ministry in Iran
candidates.summary: MNN interview with Lana Silk: Transform Iran's Kairos chatbot (Bible-based answers from a vetted apologetics library, 24/7 human oversight, anonymous, free VPN) is now used in ~172 countries and 27 of the top 30 Open Doors World Watch List countries; it points users toward pastors, reconciliation and therapy.
candidates.organization: Transform Iran (reported by Mission Network News)

candidates.title: A surprising number of Americans use AI for spiritual reasons. Here's what they told us
candidates.summary: NPR/Ipsos poll: among AI users, 11% sought spiritual guidance, 13% generated prayers, 15% used it to study Scripture; nearly 7 in 10 say they never would seek spiritual guidance from AI.
candidates.whyNotChosen: Survey data rather than a ministry story; used as supporting context and the wisdom concern.

candidates.title: Nashville team uses AI to convert whole Bible into musical form
candidates.summary: Music Bible / TheSinging.Bible: ~70-person Nashville team set the full Bible text to AI-generated music in 11 genres, no words changed.
candidates.whyNotChosen: Launched late August (RNS 2026-09-09 already reported 1M plays); in-window coverage is largely a press-release rewrite (newswire.com).

candidates.title: Vietnamese priest trains clergy and lay leaders to use AI in pastoral ministry
candidates.summary: Camillian priest representing Vietnam's bishops at the First Asian Catholic Digital Missionary Assembly; stresses human encounter.
candidates.organization: Herald Malaysia / Catholic Bishops' Conference of Vietnam
candidates.whyNotChosen: Article URL not resolved (only Google News redirect seen); profile rather than a development.
